en.text: A set is a collection of well-defined objects. A ⊆ B when every element of A is in B. A ∪ B joins the elements of both sets. A ∩ B keeps only the shared elements.

Summary for unit one
paras: A set is a collection of well-defined objects. Its objects are called members or elements.
A set with no element is the empty set.
Two sets are equal if they have exactly the same elements.

screens.title: Key words of the unit
defs: A ⊆ B when every element of A is also in B.
A ∪ B: all elements in A or B or both.
A ∩ B: all elements in both A and B.

pairs: elements in A or B or both
elements in both A and B
every element of A is in B
screens.why:
∪ (union) joins: elements in A or B or both.
∩ (intersection) keeps the shared part: in both A and B.
⊆ (subset): every element of A is in B.
↔ (equivalent): same number of elements.
∅ is the empty set: no element.
screens.clue: Union joins, intersection keeps the shared part.
screens.title: Match each symbol to its meaning

screens.text: Subsets: true or false? A set is a subset of itself.
screens.why:
A ⊆ B means every element of A is in B.
Every element of A is, of course, in A.
So A ⊆ A for any set A.
True.

screens.text: Subset? True or false: {m, n, o} ⊆ {m, n}
screens.why:
Check each element of {m, n, o}.
m and n are in {m, n}.
o ∉ {m, n}.
One missing element is enough. False.
screens.clue: Is every element of the first set in the second?

screens.text: Find the intersection: A = {1, 2, 3, 4} and B = {2, 4, 6}. Tap every element of A ∩ B.
screens.why:
Check each element of A in B = {2, 4, 6}.
1 ∉ B, 2 ∈ B, 3 ∉ B, 4 ∈ B.
A ∩ B = {2, 4}.
6 is only in B.

Bracket first: A ∩ B = {4, 5}.
Then keep what is also in C = {5, 6, 7}.
4 ∉ C, 5 ∈ C.
(A ∩ B) ∩ C = {5}.
screens.clue: Do the bracket first, then intersect with C.

items.text: Review: true or false? All equivalent sets are equal sets.
items.why:
Try {1, 2} and {a, b}.
Both have 2 elements, so they are equivalent.
Their elements differ, so they are not equal.
False.
items.clue: Equivalent only needs the same count.

items.text: Review: true or false? A set is a subset of itself.
items.why:
Every element of A is in A.
So A ⊆ A.
True. (But A is not a proper subset of itself.)

items.text: Review: subset? True or false: {m, n, o} ⊆ {m, n}
items.why:
m ∈ {m, n} and n ∈ {m, n}.
o ∉ {m, n}.
Not every element is in the second set.
False.

The elements are 0, 4 and 12.
2 is not listed.
So 2 ∉ the set.
False.

items.text: Proper subsets: which one is NOT a proper subset of {e, f}?
items.why:
Proper subsets leave out at least one element.
{ } leaves out both, {e} leaves out f, {f} leaves out e.
{e, f} leaves out nothing: it is the set itself.
So {e, f} is not a proper subset of {e, f}.

items.text: Equivalent sets: which one is equivalent to the set {a, 3}?
items.why:
{a, 3} has 2 elements.
{ } has 0; {a} and {3} have 1.
{2, 3} has 2.
So {2, 3} ↔ {a, 3}.

items.text: Subsets and intersection: if A ⊆ B, which one is necessarily true?
items.why:
A ⊆ B: every element of A is in B.
So the shared part is all of A: A ∩ B = A.
A ∩ B = B and A ∪ B = A fail when B has extra elements.
A ⊂ B fails when A = B.

items.text: Find the intersection: if A = {a, b} and B = {c, d}, then A ∩ B is:
items.why:
Check a and b in B = {c, d}.
Neither is there.
A ∩ B = { }.
{a, b, c, d} is A ∪ B, a tempting wrong choice.

items.text: Venn diagrams: which diagram shows E ⊂ F?
items.why:
E ⊂ F: every element of E is in F.
F also has extra elements.
So E is the smaller set, drawn inside.
Circle E inside circle F.
